# Thirukkural Tamil Dataset

> The Tamil text of all 1,330 kurals of Thiruvalluvar's Thirukkural (திருக்குறள்), with permanent ids tk:0001 to tk:1330, each with its sources, verification status and sha256. English translations, Parimelazhagar's Tamil commentary and metre are separate tables joined by kural id. Core licence CC0-1.0.

Also known as: Tirukkural, Thirukural, Thiruvalluvar's Kural.

- Repository: https://github.com/ashwingopalsamy/thirukkural-tamil-dataset
- Website: https://thirukkural.ashwingopalsamy.in/ (one page per kural at /kural/<number>/ and per chapter at /chapter/<number>/)
- Version: 1.0.0, released 2026-10-20
- kurals_root_sha256: 86d8d109697176ee8d15150255c76265cbb5a067546215210c974fee49c6a1df
- Maintainer: Ashwin Gopalsamy, https://ashwingopalsamy.in

## Counts

- 1,330 kurals in 133 chapters (adhikarams) of ten, in three books (paal): அறத்துப்பால் (chapters 1 to 38), பொருட்பால் (39 to 108), காமத்துப்பால் (109 to 133).
- text_status: 70 verified_scan, 78 adjudicated, 1,182 verified_digital_only.
- 103 rulings in the ledger: 85 on kural text, 18 on names.
- 1,316 kurals located on their page in all three printed editions.
- 9,309 metrical feet (seer). 1,323 kurals scan as kural venba under checker v0.3; 1,293 under v0.1.
- 118 English chapter titles, as printed in Pope 1886.
- 4,206 attested readings in the variants atlas.
- 5,523 evaluation tasks; 2,660 KuralBench-lite items.

## Text status

- verified_scan: the printed editions settle the reading.
- adjudicated: a ruling in the ledger settles the reading; adjudication_ids names it.
- verified_digital_only: every digital source has the same letters; not compared letter by letter with a print.

Sources: six digital sources in three lineage groups (Hugging Face datasets aitamilnadu, Chandrasekar, Selvakumar, yuvaraj; Tamil Wikisource மூலம் and Parimelazhagar pages) and three printed editions (Pope 1886, Lazarus and Mrugesa Mudaliyar 1885, Arumuga Navalar), scanned on archive.org.

## Tables

24 tables. Source files are JSONL under data/ (text, layers, derived, signature, task and agent tables) and JSON under provenance/ (ledger, registry, reports) in the repository. `python -m tkcore.release` writes every table as Parquet to dist/hf/data/<table>.parquet.

Text (CC0-1.0):
- kurals: id, number, paal_number, paal_name_ta, iyal_number, iyal_name_ta, adhikaram_number, adhikaram_name_ta, adhikaram_name_en, position, lines_ta, text_ta, text_sha256, text_status, adjudication_ids, provenance
- adhikarams: number, name_ta, name_en, paal_number, paal_name_ta, iyal_number, iyal_name_ta, first_kural, last_kural, provenance
- divisions: level, scheme, number, paal_number, first_adhikaram, last_adhikaram, name_ta, canonical, provenance

English translations (CC0-1.0, public domain), one row per kural:
- pope1886_en: G. U. Pope, verse translation, 1886
- drew_lazarus_en: W. H. Drew (1 to 630) and John Lazarus (631 to 1330), prose translation
- aiyar1916_en: V. V. S. Aiyar, The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar, 1916
- Fields: kural_id, kural_number, text, coverage, lang, author, work_title, source_id, locator, source_sha256, carrier_license, rights, print_edition, print_leaf, print_match_share, print_match, print_note, book_match_share, text_flags, model_generated (aiyar1916_en adds tier, pdf_page)

Commentary:
- parimelazhagar_ta (MIT): Parimelazhagar's Tamil commentary, same fields as the translations
- parimelazhagar_ta_sa (CC-BY-SA-4.0): the 5 commentary rows parimelazhagar_ta withholds, from Tamil Wikisource
- parimelazhagar_struct (MIT): the commentary parsed by rule: pada_urai (word glosses), turai, group_end, summary, reported_readings, other_commentators, figures, grammar_notes, cites_works

Metre and sound (CC0-1.0):
- seer: kural_id, line, position, word, scansion_form, asai, pattern, foot, foot_ta, foot_ok
- derived: metre_ok, scansion_ok, scansion_method, scansion_note, form_ok, search_lines_ta, translit_iso15919, translit_plain, letters_per_line
- sound_index: letters_per_line, asai_pattern, seer_pattern, monai, edukai, end_rhyme

Readings and links:
- variants_atlas (CC0-1.0): kural_id, reading_id, text, status, same_letters_as_canonical, ledger_id, sources
- variants_atlas_sa (CC-BY-SA-4.0): readings carried only under CC-BY-SA-4.0
- quote_keys (CC0-1.0): text_sha256, compare_key, line1_key, line2_key, opening_key, citation_ta, citation_en, permalink
- echo_graph (CC0-1.0): source, target, kind, weight, shared_keys

Evaluation (CC0-1.0, every row carries a canary string):
- tasks: task_id, kural_id, type, prompt_ta, choices, answer
- kuralbench_lite: task_id, task, kural_id, prompt, target_ta

Agents (CC0-1.0):
- agent_card: one JSON object per kural for an agent to pass to a model
- merkle_proofs: leaf_index, tree_size, exact_path, letters_path (RFC 9162)

Evidence (CC0-1.0):
- ledger: ledger_id, subject, field, decision, value, candidates, evidence, adjudicator, decided_at, rationale, supersedes
- sources: source_id, title, kind, lineage_group, url, revision, declared_license, files
- scan_locations: kural_id, edition, archive_item, leaf, image_file, bbox, located_confidently

Vectors (MIT):
- embeddings_bge_m3: one BAAI/bge-m3 vector per kural (1,024 dimensions), model_generated true on every row. The only model output in the dataset.

## Licences

- CC0-1.0: the Tamil text, structure, the three English translations and 19 of the 24 tables.
- MIT: parimelazhagar_ta and parimelazhagar_struct (the carrier's terms), embeddings_bge_m3 (the model's declared licence).
- CC-BY-SA-4.0: parimelazhagar_ta_sa and variants_atlas_sa.

## Load

pandas:

```python
import pandas as pd
base = "https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ashwingopalsamy/thirukkural-tamil-dataset/main"
kurals = pd.read_json(f"{base}/data/core/kurals.jsonl", lines=True)
pope = pd.read_json(f"{base}/data/layers/pope1886-en.jsonl", lines=True)
both = kurals.merge(pope, left_on="id", right_on="kural_id")
```

Hugging Face datasets:

```python
from datasets import load_dataset
kurals = load_dataset("json", data_files=f"{base}/data/core/kurals.jsonl", split="train")
```

text_sha256 is the sha256 of the two lines joined by a newline, in NFC, as UTF-8:

```python
import hashlib, unicodedata
k = kurals[kurals.id == "tk:0034"].iloc[0]
text_sha256 = hashlib.sha256(unicodedata.normalize("NFC", "\n".join(k.lines_ta)).encode()).hexdigest()
assert text_sha256 == "5faee0bcb2efc501ba55522190813002c1863f130a8760061243f4bdaf862b4e"
```

## Tools

Four read-only tools. Every string they return is copied from the tables, with a Merkle proof.

- find_kural: a Tamil quote of any quality -> ranked kurals with the canonical text
- get_kural: a number, 1 to 1330 -> text, chapter, transliteration, citation, translations, proof
- verify_quote: a quote, and the number it claims -> exact, same_letters, known_reading, misquote or not_found, with the words that differ
- search_english: English words -> kurals whose Pope or Drew/Lazarus translation matches

MCP: `python -m tkcore.mcp_server`, registered as `{"mcpServers": {"thirukkural": {"command": "python", "args": ["-m", "tkcore.mcp_server"]}}}`.
HTTP: `python -m tkcore.agent_tools serve`, POST /v1/<tool>, described in agents/openapi.json (OpenAPI 3.1).
Tool definitions: agents/tools.json (input_schema) and agents/tools.openai.json (strict). JSON Schemas: agents/schemas/.

## Citation

```bibtex
@dataset{gopalsamy_thirukkural_2026,
  author  = {Gopalsamy, Ashwin},
  title   = {Thirukkural Tamil Dataset},
  year    = {2026},
  version = {1.0.0},
  url     = {https://github.com/ashwingopalsamy/thirukkural-tamil-dataset}
}
```

To cite one kural, give its id and text_sha256, for example kural 34, tk:0034, 5faee0bcb2efc501ba55522190813002c1863f130a8760061243f4bdaf862b4e.
